title: Agent capability-gap sample
scope: Results describe the supplied sample, not the model’s intelligence.

sample.classification: Each entry receives one primary task category. Interface repair is classified as visual design; tool use is not inferred from task intent.
sample.limitations: Requests reveal task exposure; explicit corrections reveal reported friction. Successful performance cannot be independently established.

rating_rubric.Developing: At least two relevant entries, but insufficient outcome evidence to establish coverage or an explicit weakness. This is an evidence-status label, not a demonstrated proficiency level.
rating_rubric.Covered: At least two relevant entries with affirmative evidence of successful delivery and no material unresolved friction.
rating_rubric.Weak: At least two relevant entries and explicit friction, without the repeated broad failures required for Critical.
rating_rubric.Critical: At least two relevant entries with repeated explicit friction across multiple quality dimensions; a priority within this sample, not a universal capability judgment.

strongest_measured_task_category.status: Provisional relative candidate; no demonstrated strongest performer.
strongest_measured_task_category.basis: Among categories meeting the evidence threshold, coding alone has no explicit reported agent friction. This does not establish success, and task frequency is not used as evidence of strength.

categories.evidence: One correction explicitly reports omitted source verification. Two other requests seek authoritative sources or citations; they do not establish successful verification.
One request concerns inspecting column totals, below the minimum evidence threshold.
Three entries report poor brand alignment, a broken responsive layout, or repeated disregard of the existing interface. A fourth requests a visual asset without reporting an outcome.

Requests cover defect repair with regression tests, caching, refactoring, and migration tooling. No entry confirms delivery or test results; requesting a bug fix alone is not evidence of agent failure.
No dedicated writing tasks are present. Requests for citations are classified as research.
No tool calls or execution results are supplied. Tasks that could use tools do not independently measure execution.

surprising_weakness.finding: Brand and interface consistency remain a repeated problem despite requests spanning substantial implementation work.
surprising_weakness.evidence: Three visual entries explicitly report dissatisfaction or defects; one indicates the existing interface was disregarded again.
surprising_weakness.qualification: The contrast concerns the task mix and reported friction, not proven coding competence.

recommendation_status: These skills are relevant recommendations, not confirmed missing installations.

recommended_skills.reason: Ground changes in the current interface to address repeated brand and interface inconsistency.
Reuse approved visual assets in response to explicit asset-reuse and brand-alignment feedback.
Apply a structured audit and refinement workflow to layout, hierarchy, and responsive defects.
Retrieve authoritative source material for verification and citations; retrieval must still be followed by checking the claim against the source.
